title: The Transfiguration (6 August)
hookLine: the mountain of light, on the same date as Hiroshima's bombing

lines: HIS FACE SHINES LIKE THE SUN.
cards: Three fishermen climb behind their teacher up a high mountain, apart from everyone: Peter, James and John. Near the top, the man they've been following changes in front of them. His face shines like the sun.
His clothes go white as light. Two figures from the old stories stand there talking with him. And Peter, who Mark says did not know what to say, offers to build some shelters.
The church remembers that mountain on the sixth of August. In a later century, that same date became the day an atomic bomb fell on the city of Hiroshima. One date, two lights.

teach.h: HIS FACE DID SHINE AS THE SUN.
teach.b: Matthew, Mark and Luke all tell this story. Here's Matthew, in the King James Bible: Jesus "was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light."
Transfigured means his form changed. Not a costume, not a trick of the sunset. Then Moses and Elijah appear, Elias in the King James, talking with him.
Some readers hear the law and the prophets in those two.

teach.h: PETER WANTS TO BUILD THREE TENTS.
teach.b: Peter blurts out: "Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias." He wants to keep the moment, to pitch a tent around it.
Before he finishes, a bright cloud covers them, and a voice says: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." The disciples fall on their faces, terrified.
Then Jesus touches them: "Arise, and be not afraid." They look up and "saw no man, save Jesus only." Then they walk back down, into ordinary need.
Orthodox, Catholic and some Protestant calendars keep this feast.

And the date now carries a second light. On the day the church reads of a light that ends with be not afraid, a light that burns made a whole city afraid. Some churches mark both together, with prayer for peace.
The story doesn't make that second light smaller. It stands beside it.

how: Orthodox, Catholic and some Protestant churches keep the Transfiguration on the sixth of August with readings of the mountain story, and some churches join it with prayers for peace because it shares the date of the Hiroshima bombing.

games.q: you're Peter. your teacher is shining like the sun, and Moses and Elias are beside him. what do you say?
o: let's run down and tell everyone.
games.why: Peter offers to make three tabernacles. before he finishes, a bright cloud covers them and a voice says, hear ye him.

practice: Name one place where people are afraid tonight because of war; don't search for the worst image, just name the place. Then picture Jesus touching his friends on the mountain, and the words, arise, and be not afraid.
If you pray, offer Jesus's words from the Sermon on the Mount, blessed are the peacemakers; if you don't, hold that place and its people quietly for the length of the sit.

wordCard.voice: The Transfiguration. The moment on the mountain when Jesus's face shone like the sun, and a voice said, hear ye him. Kept on the sixth of August.

orig.note: Greek, Matthew 17:2: he was transfigured, his form was changed.
